alanian_kingdom.NationalPersonality: Mounted prestige, kinship obligations and fair distribution sustain leadership more than commands from a permanent court. Beler must protect families, herds and seasonal pasture to retain followers. alanian_kingdom.LongTermStrategy:
First secure the approaches to Uspe and seasonal movement between the Don and Kuban. Scout toward the Huns and disperse families and remounts; a prestigious lancer charge is not worth exposing every herd and winter camp.

Seek Gothic and Caucasian support through cavalry cooperation, marriage ties and reciprocal passage. Despite the current war with the Bosporans, retain the option of a truce for grain and access to port markets. Measure gains in livestock, provisions and dependable escort rather than an imagined Roman tax treasury.

Mobilization depends on fodder, season and agreement among kin groups. Concentrating requisitions on their horses risks losing followers. If the eastern position fails, preserve people and herds, then mountain escape routes, and negotiate subordinate status or paid service if necessary. Beler and the other chiefs must agree the terms, rather than one household binding the entire coalition.

War with Huns and Bosporans threatens different approaches; Gothic and Caucasian cooperation can share warning duties.

Some chiefs favor holding pasture while others seek movement or bounded service for security. Beler must define common burdens and rewards.

Followers value bargaining, household survival and freedom from powerful neighbors. antean_kingdom.LongTermStrategy:

Exchange grain, ironwork and warnings with other woodland groups. Envoys, passage agreements and hostages can restrain mounted raiders; agree household contributions of food and fighters before collecting them.

Fighters also cultivate the fields, so prolonged mobilization consumes seed reserves and divides kin. If outer settlements become untenable, move families and grain into tributary country and seek a truce. Bozh must preserve the ability to regroup and not let personal prestige prevent a necessary withdrawal.

Sarmatians are the current enemy; friendly Sclaveni and Venedians can negotiate passage.

Villages have different levy capacities. Bozh needs agreed limits of help, captive recovery and food sharing.
